description: Four oscillators — a sine, a triangle, a saw and a square — each with its own waveshaping control and its own rate range, plus a bank of four noise colours

params.text: Sets that channel's frequency: 15Hz to 1000Hz in VCO mode with coarse tuning, 0.15Hz to 10Hz in LFO mode with coarse tuning, and a twelfth of a semitone either side of C0 in fine tuning
Folds the sine wave back on itself, adding harmonics as it is turned up
Hardens the triangle towards a squarer shape by clipping it at a rising gain
Offsets a copy of the saw and subtracts a tenth of it, which thins and phases the waveform
Sets the width of the square wave, from half at fully counter-clockwise down to a twentieth at fully clockwise
Switched to VCO that channel runs at audio rates, switched to LFO at modulation rates
Switched to V/OCT that channel's frequency input is read as a volt-per-octave pitch; switched to FM it is read as linear frequency modulation, AC coupled and scaled at 120Hz per volt
Switched to FINE that channel's frequency knob covers a twelfth of a semitone either side of C0 instead of its full range, and the knob jumps to the centre of that range as you switch

inputs.text: Sets that channel's pitch or modulates its frequency, according to that channel's FM type switch; leave it unpatched and the channel takes whatever reached the input above it
Modulates that channel's waveshaping control; a tenth of a volt moves it a hundredth of the way, and the result is added to the knob and held inside its range

outputs.text: Pink noise, falling at -3dB per octave
Blue noise, rising at +3dB per octave
Brown noise, falling at -6dB per octave, with its very low end filtered out

notes: the four frequency inputs cascade: a channel with nothing patched reads the channel above it, and channel 1 with nothing patched reads 0V. Patch one and every channel below it follows.
switching a channel to FINE moves its frequency knob to the middle of the fine range, so the pitch it had at coarse tuning is not kept.
the noise outputs are only computed while something is patched to them, so an unpatched noise jack costs nothing.
menu: Oversampling: Off, x2, x4, x8 — runs the oscillators above the sample rate to cut aliasing; x2 by default, and found on the Anti-aliasing submenu
Use ADAA — turns on antiderivative antialiasing in the waveshapers; on by default, and found on the Anti-aliasing submenu
Remove Pulse DC Offset — takes the DC offset out of the square output when its width is away from half; on by default
